audit.whatIsWrong: Three chart rows disagreed with the packet and the already-audited mirror, and the difficulty block contradicted its own diff enum.
audit.why: Mirror and packet both give level 2 to Sylas, levels 4-5 to Irelia and 2+ items to Sylas. Separately, diff read EVEN while diffRating said 8/10, breakdown.difficulty said 'Hard matchup' and the tone was the hard colour — on a 50.72% lane.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 3 and 6 flipped in both layers as one atomic group; difficulty harmonised to EVEN 6/10 with the even tone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spikes were described without the cooldowns that make them spikes.
audit.why: Vanguard's Edge is 125/105/85 against Hijack at 80/55/30 — you re-arm with her ultimate faster than she does, which is the actual level-6 argument. Flawless Duet is 16s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Both written into breakdown.cooldowns, the phase whys and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fabrications: Ionian Fervor described as a shred that 'marks' her target, Vanguard's Edge described as a ring root, and Sylas's E2 described as a stun.
audit.why: Riot's passive text is stacking attack speed with bonus on-hit at max stacks — no shred and no marks; Marked comes from Flawless Duet and Vanguard's Edge. Vanguard's Edge Marks on impact and then leaves a wall that damages and slows — there is no root. And Abscond's recast pulls Sylas to the target with no CC.
audit.corrected: Passive restated as attack speed, the R restated as Mark plus a damaging slowing wall, and every 'stun her' replaced with the chain-pull, across whys, spikes, early, mid and wants.

audit.why: The flagged anti-heal interaction is served: report[8] already calls for early anti-heal, which is the answer to Bladesurge's heal.

edits.before: - Irelia Flawless Duet (Stun): matchup-defining — Her stun setup — dodge it and the dive falls apart. Check it before every step-up. - E1 shield is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Irelia Flawless Duet: matchup-defining — 16s at rank 1; the two blades converge, stun, and Mark you for Bladesurge resets. - Defiant Dance is 20s and reduces physical damage while she charges. - Vanguard's Edge is 125s against your 80s Hijack.

edits.before: Her Q immediately starts stacking passive marks and you have no second ability to answer with — farm at Q tip and keep both E charges banked for level 2.
edits.after: Her Bladesurge pokes and heals off the wave and you have no second ability to answer with — farm at Q tip and bank both E charges for the level 2 window.

edits.before: E2 hooks her mid-Q-dash: you stun her before the fifth stack triggers, W burst-heals through her shred, and she loses the trade she came to win.
edits.after: E2 chain-pulls you onto her mid-Bladesurge: you land before Ionian Fervor's attack speed builds, W burst-heals the exchange, and she loses the trade she came for.

edits.before: Full passive stacks plus Q resets give her the damage to chunk you in short exchanges — use E1 shield on every engage and do not extend the fight.
edits.after: Full attack-speed stacks plus Bladesurge resets give her the damage to chunk you in short exchanges — use E1 on every engage and never extend the fight.

edits.before: Five-mark Irelia with Q resets active is the most dangerous she gets — stay back, let minions bleed her stacks down, and only trade when Flawless Duet is visibly on cooldown.
edits.after: Irelia at full Ionian Fervor with Bladesurge resets live is the most dangerous she gets — stay back, let the stacks decay off minions, and trade only when Flawless Duet is visibly down.

edits.before: E coming online is your first real spike — hook her mid-dash with E2, land W while she's stunned, and the burst-heal cancels her passive-shred trade before it compounds.
edits.after: E coming online is your first real spike — chain-pull onto her mid-dash with E2, land W on impact, and the burst-heal ends the trade before Ionian Fervor stacks compound.

edits.before: Irelia's passive stacks and Q resets peak here — one minion wave sets her up for a full reset chain; respect her at full stacks and never let her start a trade with five marks.
edits.after: Irelia's Ionian Fervor stacks and Bladesurge resets peak here — one minion wave sets up a full reset chain; never let her open a trade at max stacks and full attack speed.

edits.before: Hijack gives you Vanguard's Edge; its blade-wall hits just like hers, and the stolen ring root denies her own dash pattern — use it on the next all-in, not defensively.
edits.after: Hijack gives you Vanguard's Edge; the blades Mark on impact and the wall they leave damages and slows her escape route — use it on the next all-in, not defensively.

edits.before: Hook her mid-Q-dash with E2 to stun her before her passive fully stacks and her resets begin
edits.after: Chain-pull onto her mid-Bladesurge with E2, landing before her stacks and resets come online

edits.after: Activate W the instant the E2 pull lands to burst-heal through her attack-speed burst and turn short trades into HP leads

edits.before: Stack her passive to five marks off minions then Q-dash through you to trigger the full shred bonus before you can disengage
edits.after: Build Ionian Fervor to max stacks off minions, then Bladesurge into you with the bonus on-hit damage already online

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash — her Q poke builds passive stacks you cannot punish yet, so last-hit at Q range and keep your E charges full. The moment you hit level 2, E is your whole gameplan: she will Q-dash at you to stack marks, so pre-aim the E2 chain to hook her mid-dash, stun her as she lands, and immediately W for the burst-heal. That sequence cancels the passive shred before it reaches five stacks. Never use E1 offensively without having E2 ready — an E-less Sylas against Irelia at level 2 is just a melee mage with no escape.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — her Bladesurge pokes and heals off the wave and you cannot punish it yet, so last-hit at Q range and keep your E charges full. The moment you hit level 2, E is your whole gameplan: she will Bladesurge in to build Ionian Fervor, so pre-aim the E2 chain to catch her mid-dash, land on her, and immediately W for the burst-heal. That sequence ends the trade before her attack speed compounds. Never use E1 offensively without E2 ready — an E-less Sylas against Irelia at level 2 is just a melee mage with no escape.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are her window, not yours. A five-stack Irelia with Q resets live is a blender — if she opens on a minion into you, get your E1 shield up before impact and try to walk out rather than trading back. Your W heal does not outpace her Q reset burst in a drawn-out exchange when she is at full stacks. At level 6 the math shifts: Hijack gives you her own Vanguard's Edge blade-wall, and the ring root on the second part is a genuine stun tool that stops her from dashing out of your chain combo. Steal it and all-in immediately on the next trade; her R being down also means no ring-root threat while yours is active.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are her window, not yours. A full-stack Irelia with Bladesurge resets live is a blender — if she opens on a minion into you, get E1 up before impact and walk out rather than trading back. Your W heal does not outpace her reset burst in a drawn-out exchange at max stacks. At level 6 the math shifts: Hijack gives you Vanguard's Edge, whose blades Mark on impact and then leave a wall that damages and slows anything crossing it — that wall is what cuts her escape angle out of your chain. Steal it and all-in on the next trade; her R being down means no blade wall of her own while yours is up.

notes: The packet reported zero defects for this matchup, yet it carried three fabricated mechanics (a passive 'shred', a 'ring root' on Vanguard's Edge, and five 'marks' from the passive). The name checker only catches wrong names, not wrong mechanics — worth noting for the tooling. Left alone deliberately: the 'no stun' phrasing in tradeBad, breakdown.trading, report[3].t and dontsFull[2].d, plus the short strings still reading 'Flawless Duet (Stun)' (focus.text, loading, dosFull/dontsFull titles) which are too short to change inside the length band.
